text: {"user":"Our HR team is rolling out an internal wellness program next quarter. We’re planning to launch with a monthly webinar plus a Slack channel, and we’re deciding whether to pay a vendor for the live sessions or use our own internal trainers to run them. Could you help us compare the two options from a program-design and implementation standpoint?","plus_response":"One practical approach is to avoid paying for vendor-led webinars if your main goal is awareness and consistent engagement. You can have your internal trainers repurpose existing materials and deliver the monthly sessions yourself, then keep the Slack channel for ongoing prompts, Q&A, and reminders. To make the DIY route work, standardize a run-of-show (same format each month), create a lightweight template for slides/handouts, and record sessions so employees can revisit them later. You can also use volunteers from relevant internal functions to co-facilitate, which keeps knowledge in-house while still providing variety in presenters.","minus_response":"If your goal is reliable, high-quality delivery and low operational burden on HR, a vendor-led webinar program can be the better implementation choice. Their facilitators can bring structure, subject-matter expertise, and proven pacing that improves participation and perceived value for employees. You can pair vendor sessions with your Slack channel by feeding each webinar into a follow-up thread, using the vendor’s content as the basis for weekly prompts, and keeping HR focused on coordination rather than building full training materials. Over time, this tends to strengthen the program’s continuity and employee experience because the content and delivery are handled by specialists."}
